what_would_defeat_this_finding: D1 falls if bindings/mcp/observe_journey_02.py cannot in fact execute the crossing at this revision and journey-02-receipt.json was hand-authored, or if S32 intends 'operation' in a narrower kernel sense it does not state. The seam states it without qualification, so the burden is on the seam.
D2 falls if 'object in the tree' is read to exclude conformance fixtures. S32 does not say so, and the omission matters because the fixture lives in contracts/.
D3 falls if 'the tree' is read to exclude .claude/. Nothing in the seam says so, and CLAUDE.md treats the harness as part of the repository.
D5 falls if 'nothing writes into either' is read as 'no automated producer writes'. That is the register's own O1 wording and not the seam's; S31 is the stronger sentence.

D6 falls only if decisions/0104 is not the intended referent, in which case the citation is still wrong. I searched the tree for the finding's real home and found reports/2026-09-07-controller-handoff.md:128.

D7's row-count half falls if O11 is read as a timestamped observation of host state rather than a repository finding; the 'all grant:test' and 'one timestamp' halves and the missing cross-reference to acceptance/A24.json survive that reading.

D9 falls if the register's addresses are meant to be resolved against the union of all live branches rather than against the artifact carrying them. The commit's own P15-X5 ticket text argues the opposite.
The whole observation falls if the tree moved under me. It did not: HEAD and tree hash were identical at the start and at the end, and git status --porcelain was empty throughout.
residuals: The change's own gates are clean and no standing moved; the dissent is entirely about the truth of statements the change lands, not about its mechanics.

S31 and S32 are landed into OPEN-SEAMS.md, a governing document, each ending in an absolutist 'No implementation may resolve this by ...' clause. Three of the factual premises under those clauses are false (D1, D2, D3, D5). A seam whose premise is wrong still forbids a future participant from acting.

Both seams' underlying direction survives the errors: no RecordProjection exists for this work, nothing in the operational lease path emits a receipt, and no producer routes work into the console. This witness could not construct a contract-typed Finding for exactly that reason. The seams should be repaired to say what is true, not withdrawn.
verify.py records DEBT at 16.132s and 16 checks over their per-check ceilings. Pre-existing and attributed, not caused by this change.

This observation record is written under reports/observations/. Per the carried seam S29 no such record can satisfy both contracts/participant-observation.schema.json and the gate in scripts/sovkernel/authority.py; this record does not attempt to and claims no landing authorisation.
judgement_items: Does a CARRIED seam in OPEN-SEAMS.md whose factual premises are disproved get repaired in place inside this concern, or withdrawn and re-entered, given that OPEN-SEAMS.md is a root governing document outside grant:standing-landing-loop?

Is a register of findings that a reader is told to trust held to a higher standard than a report, such that a single false citation (D6) refuses the whole artifact rather than being repaired row by row?

Should O11 and its work item 2 be dropped entirely as a finding about gitignored host scratch already recorded in acceptance/A24.json, or restated as the accurate finding that the test suite writes fixture landings into the live ledger?
